links.outcome: AI performance on local consecutive low-prevalence primary care CXR cohort against CT reference
links.effect: AUROC 0.648 (95% CI 0.630-0.665), sensitivity 35.3%, specificity 94.2%; prevalence of significant lesions 2.2% (68 of 3047)
links.quote: The performance of commercial AI in these high-volume, low-prevalence settings was poorer than expected, although it modestly boosted the performance of less-experienced readers.

links.outcome: Reader AUROC with versus without AI assistance, and reading time
links.effect: Readers' AUROCs ranged 0.534-0.676 without AI and 0.571-0.688 with AI (all p<0.05); reading time 2.96-10.27 s longer with AI.
links.quote: The readers' AUROCs ranged from 0.534-0.676 without AI and 0.571-0.688 with AI (all p values < 0.05).

links.outcome: Performance drop when applying AI in a setting differing from its training setting
links.effect: AI performance in low-prevalence health screening was poorer than expected, suggesting experimental/regulatory performance may not translate to real-world practice.
links.quote: The technical prowess of AI demonstrated in experimental settings and approved by regulatory bodies may not directly translate to real-world practice, especially where the demand for AI assistance is highest.
